summary: 63-year-old diabetic smoker, 2 h epigastric 'indigestion' with sweating and vomiting, HR 52, BP 98/60, soft non-tender abdomen; no ECG recorded yet.

inputs.hpi: 2 hours of heavy epigastric pain he calls 'indigestion', with nausea, one vomit and sweating. Antacid did not help. Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, smoker. No chest pain described.

exam.general: Grey, clammy, sweaty. Temperature 36.6°C, pulse 52/min, BP 98/60, RR 20, SpO2 95%.
exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no guarding. Bowel sounds normal.
exam.cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, no murmur. JVP not raised.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (inferior myocardial infarction)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Epigastric pain with diaphoresis, bradycardia and borderline hypotension in a diabetic smoker: acute coronary syndrome (inferior MI) until proven otherwise. 12-lead ECG now, troponin, emergency services.

mustNotMiss.note: Epigastric pain + diaphoresis + bradycardia/hypotension in a diabetic smoker: inferior MI must be on the displayed differential.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: Symptom inference top 5 has no ACS/STEMI (pancreatitis ×2, perforated ulcer, gastroenteritis, gastric carcinoma): epigastric pain, sweating and vomiting do not weight the cardiac entries.

emergencyLevel.note: Web passed on 2026-09-25 only because the negative 'No chest pain described' matches the cardiac red-flag regex (no negation handling); the pass is fragile — see findings/gi-emergencies.md.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Epigastric pain and sweating' gives 'routine'.

mustInclude.note: ESC 2023: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first contact.

guideline.name: ESC guidelines — acute coronary syndromes (2023)
guideline.section: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact; hs-troponin; inferior STEMI (right-sided leads); primary PCI
guideline.citation: Byrne RA, Rossello X, Coughlan JJ, et al. 2023 ESC guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes. Eur Heart J. 2023;44:3720–826.

rationale: Dangerous mimic of upper-GI pain. A soft, non-tender abdomen with diaphoresis, bradycardia and hypotension points away from the abdomen; the engines must ask for an ECG and troponin before any GI work-up.

authoring.author: Claude (GI surgical emergencies cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Every citation is verified: false.
